result:
Everything is green: **42/42 API smoke checks, 33/33 headless E2E checks**, seed SQL validated with the real Postgres parser. The project is complete.

**What was built (iteration 1 — full stack from scratch)**

**Docker** — `docker/docker-compose.yml` with `database` (Postgres 16 + healthcheck + init scripts + named volume), `backend` (FastAPI, :8000), `frontend` (Vite build in nginx, :3000, proxies `/api`, `/auth`, `/health`, `/media` to backend). All contexts/mounts inside `/workspace`.

**Backend** (`app/backend/`) — JWT auth (PBKDF2, genuinely verified), all 17 contract endpoints at exact paths, 401 on every `/api/*` without bearer, `/health`, `/media/*` static serving with Range support (video seeking works). Per-profile privacy via `X-Profile-Id` (falls back to first profile); registration auto-creates a profile so the register→create→list→read→delete chain works for fresh users.

**Seed** (`app/database/init/`) — generated from the real `titles.json`: 60 real titles (posters/backdrops/synopses/languages), 22 genres, 666 episodes for the 32 series, top-10 ranks per kind, 6 real trailer clips assigned as `video_url`, demo user (`demo@netflix.example`/`demo1234`) with 3 profiles and seeded My List/ratings/Continue Watching. Fixed a real Postgres gotcha: explicit seed IDs don't advance identity sequences → added `setval` realignment so new registrations can't PK-collide.

**Frontend** (`app/frontend/`) — all 13 screens with the provided fonts, wordmark, and icon SVGs (paths inlined): landing collage, login (sign in/up), "Who's watching?" with full profile management, browse home (hero + the exact spec rail set), shows/movies with genre dropdowns, games (honest empty rails — no games in dataset), New & Popular (top-10 ranked numerals), genre category, title-detail modal (episodes + season selector + rate dialog), full player (play/pause, seek, ±10s, volume, next episode, episodes drawer, subs/audio menus, fullscreen, back, resume, progress reporting; large play button so blocked-autoplay headless browsers can still start playback), My List, Browse by Languages (real language data; honest empty states for dubbing/subtitles), account, search, 404.

**Verified locally** (no Docker here): backend against SQLite with the same ORM models (42-check contract suite), full user journey via Playwright/Chromium (33 checks, zero console errors), seed SQL parsed with `pglast`, Range requests, fresh-user API chain.

**Still unverified / caveats**
- The compose stack itself couldn't be booted in this sandbox — Docker build/boot is the main remaining risk.
- I cannot see the reference screenshots (no image input), so pixel fidelity is based on the spec's detailed descriptions, not direct comparison.
- No cast data exists in the dataset, so the modal omits cast (honest); Games and Coming This Week use real-data-derived content with honest empty states.
